rendered: The paper defines its C rate through the theoretical capacity of sulfur: C = 1675 mA/gS[1]. So the theoretical capacity corresponding to the paper's 1C[2] definition is the value quoted above, in sulfur-based units. On first discharge at the slow rate of 0.1C[3], the material reaches 91%[4] of theoretical capacity ("91% of theoretical capacity[5]"). Applying that share to the theoretical capacity gives a first-discharge capacity of about 1,524.25[6] mAh/gS (sulfur-based), computed as the stated share of the theoretical capacity.
